words.prose: {{ar:مَّتَٰعًۭا}} ({{tr:matāʿan}}) opens the ayah as an accusative gerund that reaches back to the prior growth catalogue and names what that catalogue has become: usable provision. Its indefinite singular form gathers many listed items into one broad provision class, while the root field keeps the benefit as enjoyed, time-bounded use rather than permanent possession, a pressure reinforced by 2:36. The local grammar selects provision and benefit from {{ar:م ت ع}} ({{tr:m-t-ʿ}}); wider derivative and branch evidence helps color the word as granted usufruct, but does not make unrelated root branches active here. Its compressed opening and long vowel give the summary noun audible breadth before the clipped beneficiary phrases, so its position and sound both hinge the movement from inventory to allocation. The human-plus-livestock provision formula is reinforced by echoes with 79:33 and 16:80.

words.prose: {{ar:لَّكُمْ}} ({{tr:lakum}}) makes the first beneficiary explicit: the provision is assigned to the addressed humans by the lām phrase. The phrase marks benefit and allocation more than unrestricted ownership, because it remains dependent on {{ar:مَّتَٰعًۭا}} ({{tr:matāʿan}}), a word of usable provision. Its fused preposition-plus-pronoun form makes the beneficiary relation compact and immediate, and the attached {{ar:كُمْ}} ({{tr:-kum}}) turns the food catalogue into direct address. Its first position foregrounds human use while the following parallel phrase prevents that use from exhausting the ayah's scope.

words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) is the small hinge that prevents the livestock phrase from collapsing into the human phrase. It coordinates a second lām-marked beneficiary under the same {{ar:مَّتَٰعًۭا}} ({{tr:matāʿan}}), so the ayah has one provision head and two recipient classes. Because the conjunction is prefixed to the second phrase, addition and allocation arrive together rather than as a detached afterthought.

The wording does not merely add a bare possessed noun after {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}); the wa-li onset makes coordination and allocation arrive together before the livestock noun. Repeating the allocation marker balances {{ar:لَّكُمْ}} ({{tr:lakum}}) and lets the animals receive provision in their own right within the same distribution. Its delayed position also makes the livestock share the structural landing of the ayah.

words.prose: {{ar:أَنْعَٰمِكُمْ}} ({{tr:anʿāmikum}}) closes the ayah by naming the livestock themselves. The noun is genitive under the repeated {{ar:لِ}} ({{tr:li}}) and definite through the attached {{ar:كُمْ}} ({{tr:-kum}}), so the animals are both beneficiaries of provision and tied to the same human addressees. The selected sense is concrete herd animals from {{ar:ن ع م}} ({{tr:n-ʿ-m}}), while the root's favor and ease field makes those animals embodied provision rather than a neutral asset list. As the final word, it resolves the prior pasture reference by naming the animal consumers. Its long-vowel and guttural echo answers the opening provision noun, while the repeated {{ar:كُمْ}} ({{tr:-kum}}) cadence and echoes at 79:33, 16:80, and 16:5 keep the livestock endpoint inside the wider human-and-livestock provision formula.

topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the livestock are grammatically recipients of provision and relationally tied to the addressed humans at the same time.
topics.reason: The local morphology and attachments directly support both relations: genitive governance by the preposition and possessive definiteness through the suffix.

evidence_checked: v4:branches B001 and B002 favor and ease
topics.reason: The local noun selects the livestock branch, so abstract blessing, delight, or bestowal forms are retained only as root-family resonance and not as replacement senses.

topics.headline: livestock are dependents receiving provision
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the animals are not only assets for humans; the construction casts them as living dependents reached by provision.
topics.reason: The repeated lām makes the livestock a beneficiary phrase, and the 16:5 comparison supports the livestock-benefit field without overriding the local syntax.

topics.headline: final word resolves pasture into animal provision
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah lands on dependent livestock, so the prior pasture item becomes visibly assigned to its consumers.
topics.reason: The final position, the coordinated beneficiary structure, and the boundary to the prior pasture item all support reading the word as the endpoint of the provision chain.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **The entire crop chain resolves into allocated use.** `مَّتَٰعًا` activates benefit enjoyed and used (`م ت ع` B001) and usable goods or provision (`م ت ع` B003); `أَنْعَٰمِكُمْ` activates grazing livestock (`ن ع م` B005). The two datives supply allocation to people and their animals; I infer that human benefit includes maintenance of dependent creatures. The ayah reads as an interspecies economy rather than exclusively human consumption.
2. **Enjoyment is temporary keeping, not self-sufficiency.** `م ت ع` B007 activates prolonged keeping for benefit, while `ن ع م` B001 activates bestowed favor. The immediate transition to the deafening event supplies an endpoint; I infer that provision is held and enjoyed for a span but cannot secure the holder against the next event. The ayah corrects 80:5's self-sufficiency by recoding possessions as granted, time-bound use.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 80:33 was the decisive correction: the deafening arrival terminates the apparent open-endedness of use. Later family-flight also shows that bestowed well-being (`ن ع م` B001) cannot be converted into permanent relational protection.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Benefit is concretized as usable provision.** `م ت ع B001` supplies benefit enjoyed and used, while `م ت ع B003` supplies goods, food, and provision meeting needs. Grain, fruit, oil-bearing trees, gardens, and fodder at 80:27-31 populate the abstract noun, and the two beneficiary phrases allocate its use. The ayah therefore reads as the functional output of the preceding production system, not as a decorative summary.

2. **Provision is temporary maintenance rather than permanent security.** `م ت ع B007` supplies prolonged keeping, life, or respite so benefit can continue. The deafening event arrives immediately at 80:33, and by 80:37 each person is occupied by an isolating affair. I infer that food sustains creatures through a limited interval but cannot prevent the transition. `مَّتَٰعًۭا` gains the temporal sense of maintenance under respite.

3. **Livestock favor turns into an image of dispersal.** `ن ع م B005` directly supplies grazing livestock, while `ن ع م B001` supplies bestowed favor: the animals and their fodder participate in one benefaction. Yet `ن ع م B008` supplies an ostrich-flight image for scattering, activated by human flight at 80:34. I infer a deliberate reversal from grazing cohesion to social dispersal. `أَنْعَٰمِكُمْ` thus closes the provision scene with a latent motion that the next scene realizes among humans.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 80:33-37 decisively bounded the benefit: arrival interrupts use, flight realizes `ن ع م B008` scattering, and private concern replaces shared maintenance. These later ayat corrected `مَّتَٰعًۭا` into respite rather than durable security.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir şeyden yarar sağlama ve haz alma eylemleriyle bunları sağlayan şeyi ortak bir çekirdekte toplar. lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım, genel eylem ve ad biçimlerini birlikte kapsar; başka dallardaki belirli kalıpların dar anlamlarını bu çekirdeğe katmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyden yarar sağlamak veya haz almak ve bu yararı ya da hazzı sağlayan şey. İyi bir durumda belli bir süre yararlanabilme düşüncesi bu çekirdeğe eşlik eder.

morphemes_tsv.note: ayah attribution taken from morpheme_id/word_id, never from the qac_ref column: basmalah rows are a000 but carry surah 1's qac_refs

word_morpheme_spans.note: word_analysis critical words are orthographic/analytic units, not QAC words; each resolves to a MORPHEME SPAN. The upstream aligned_qac_word_ref is preserved verbatim in word_analysis and is NOT corrected here -- renumbering would fabricate identities (PRINCIPLES.md §11 / basmalah no-hidden-renumbering rule). Use word_morpheme_spans for any word-level join to QAC.

word_analysis_qac_alignment.note: aligned_qac_word_ref does NOT resolve against qac_morphemes for this ayah: word-analysis counts orthographic words where QAC counts morphological words. Word-level joins between word_analysis topics and QAC morphology are UNRELIABLE here. Upstream defect in quran-data's word-analysis; deliberately not auto-repaired (renumbering would fabricate identities).

channel_review.note: first-pass blind review by a single reader; no adjudication, no accept/reject, no per-ayah channel maturity. Not a channel ledger.

channel_generated_outputs.note: Generated network-v3 channel discovery/family/path outputs are available as external quran-data files; read them only when channel detail is necessary, and do not treat them as an adjudicated channel ledger.

full_context_packet.note: surah-scope fallback: the default commentary workflow does not consume per-ayah focus packets, so the source packet is scoped by this builder to roots this ayah can justify and carries no staged reveal order

scoping.note: SCOPED, NOT ABSENT. The surah-scope fallback inventory covers every root in the surah; it is narrowed here to roots this ayah can justify -- roots occurring in this ayah (all their branches kept, unconditionally, because Layer 2 selects nothing) plus roots explicitly cited by channel material anchored here (only the cited branches kept, enough to resolve the citation). A root listed in dropped_roots is a deliberate scoping decision, not a missing source.

v12_reader_responses.note: Per-ayah focus-run reader responses are retired from the default commentary workflow. Use regular reader walks, plus/minus-5 reader walks, and cross-run publication findings for corpus-wide reader-derived evidence.

v12_focus_trace_hermetic.note: Hermetic Focus Trace not requested for this bundle. Rebuild with --include-focus-trace, or --require-focus-trace when reader JSON must be present.

v12_cross_run_publication.note: Compact final cross-run findings for this ayah, reconciled upstream from regular and plus/minus-5 reader runs; use as a coverage/priority check, not as replacement prose.

occurrence_evidence_trim.note: TRIMMED, NOT ABSENT. dictionary_entry.occurrence_evidence.occurrences and .ayahs are removed from every root by design: they are a per-occurrence QAC concordance and character-span alignment table carrying zero readings, branches or senses, and they dominated bundle size (~1.5 MB for a single common root). occurrence_evidence.summary (corpus frequency) and .forms (inflectional inventory) are retained. Dictionary/gloss branches are kept in full for every included Furuq root target.

branch_policy.note: No branch filtering is applied. Every branch present in each included dictionary/gloss root entry is kept.

root_mapping.policy: Use the dominant Furuq root for every QAC root, and include non-dominant Furuq targets as additional root_lexicon entries when qac-furuq-v4-root-map marks the QAC root as split.

root_lexicon.note: Turkish is the only language with dictionary entries/glosses currently sourced.
